gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ for over two hours.
gaps.hint: for over two hours up to now
gaps.explanation: A duration continuing up to the present moment takes the present perfect continuous: have been chatting.

gaps.sentence: He ___ very shy at first, but once you know him he is very chatty.
gaps.hint: seem describes a state not action
gaps.explanation: 'Seem' describes a state and is not used continuously: seems.

gaps.sentence: She has bought the paint, so tomorrow she ___ the kitchen.
gaps.hint: an intention already decided before speaking
gaps.explanation: An intention decided before the moment of speaking uses 'be going to': is going to paint.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather ___ walk five miles to school when he was a boy.
gaps.hint: a past habit no longer true
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' describes past habits or states that are no longer true: used to walk.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.
